items.followUp: Why is the ability to produce fertile offspring used to distinguish species of sexually reproducing organisms?

rubric.why: Shows why interbreeding is not a suitable criterion for most unicellular organisms.
rubric.description: Most unicellular organisms reproduce asexually and do not interbreed.
rubric.how: Award for stating that they reproduce asexually or do not interbreed.

rubric.why: Identifies the basis used to group these organisms into species.
rubric.description: They are grouped into species by similarities in their characteristics.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning similarities in their characteristics.

modelAnswer: The interbreeding criterion is not suitable for most unicellular organisms because they reproduce asexually and do not interbreed.
They are therefore grouped into species by similarities in their characteristics.

items.followUp: How does an enzyme-substrate complex form?

rubric.why: The substrate binds at the enzyme's active site.
rubric.description: The active site binds a specific substrate because their shapes are complementary.
rubric.how: Award for describing substrate binding at the active site or its specificity.

rubric.why: Binding at the active site enables the enzyme to catalyse the reaction.
rubric.description: Substrate binding forms an enzyme-substrate complex and allows catalysis.
rubric.how: Award for naming the complex or describing the catalytic role.

modelAnswer: The active site is the part of an enzyme where a specific substrate binds because their shapes are complementary.
This binding forms an enzyme-substrate complex, allowing the enzyme to catalyse the reaction.

items.followUp: Explain one way that excessive transpiration can damage a plant.

rubric.why: Identifies the harmful water loss caused by excessive transpiration.
rubric.description: The plant loses water faster than it can absorb it.
rubric.how: Award for stating that excessive transpiration causes water loss.

rubric.why: Names a consequence of excessive water loss.
rubric.description: Water loss may cause wilting, reduced growth or death.
rubric.how: Award for giving one valid consequence.

modelAnswer: Transpiration is harmful when it is excessive because the plant loses water faster than it can absorb it.
The plant may wilt, its growth may be reduced, and it may eventually die.
